# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Keep every `> **System**` panel from the mastered chapter, including a notice the narrator only hears. Do not turn a panel into italics, a sound effect, or narration. Do not repeat a panel. A notice the mastered chapter already shows more than once stays repeated that many times, and no more. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks. Keep a mastered thought in italics. Do not turn it into spoken dialogue.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

```text
＃327화



“가장 중요한 얘기가 남았군요. 안 그런가요?”

검을 늘어트린 주화란은 아름다웠고, 한편으로는 차가웠다.

서릿발 같은 기세가 그녀를 중심으로 솟아올라 한 사람을 향했다.

“송 표두.”

주화란의 시선을 따라 사람들의 고개가 돌아간다. 그 끝에 그가 있었다.

삼십 대 초반으로 짐작되는 사내. 나름 잘생긴 용모였지만 사납게 위로 솟구친 눈썹이 흠이다.

송일섬의 입술이 비틀림과 동시에 냉랭한 목소리가 흘러나왔다.

“지금 날 부른 거요?”

아직 다루 안에 남아 있던 사람들의 반응은 딱 두 가지였다.

송일섬이 누군지 몰라 어리둥절한 외부인들, 그리고 얼굴을 딱딱하게 굳힌 용봉표국의 표사들.

가장 먼저 앞으로 나선 총표두 허준의 얼굴에는 은은한 노기가 묻어 나왔다.

“소국주님 앞이다. 예를 갖추지 못할까.”

“예의라면 충분히 지켰소. 하지만 당신들은 십 년째 같은 말을 하는군.”

“이놈이 감히……!”

“그럼 감히 묻겠는데, 내게 이런 말을 하는 총표두는 왜 사람들 앞에서 소국주의 이름을 부르는 거요?”

“그, 그건.”

“굳이 대답할 필요는 없소. 총표두가 소국주를 어찌 부르건 상관없으니까. 다만 내게 예의를 강요하진 마시오.”

말투와 언행이 띠꺼워서 그렇지, 송일섬의 말이 틀리진 않은 모양이다.

순간 말문이 막힌 허준을 바라보는 내게 월화가 속삭였다.

“진 공자, 저 사람 잘 알아요?”

“누구요, 허준? 아니면…….”

“당연히 젊고 잘생긴 쪽이지. 용봉표국의 총표두야 이미 알고 있고.”

“……그런데 왜 저한테 물어봐요? 다른 사람도 아니고 하오문 섬서 지부장씩이나 되시는 분이.”

“나를 높게 평가해 주는 건 좋은데, 부임한 지 반년도 안 된 지부장이 뭘 얼마나 알겠어? 알려진 명문 대파의 제자라면 모를까, 일개 표사까지 알기에는 나도 벅차요.”

“일개 표사라……. 저자가 누구인지는 압니까?”

“음. 용봉삼표(龍鳳三鏢)에 젊고 성격 나쁜 표사 한 명이 있다는 것 정도?”

송일섬. 직책은 표두. 저자에 대해 내가 아는 것도 딱 그 정도다.

하지만 나는 월화가 모르는 한 가지를 더 알고 있었다. 바로 송일섬의 실력이다.

‘상당한 고수다. 십봉룡 이상이야.’

무림과 현대를 오가며 매번 깨닫게 되는 사실이 있다면, 레벨이 절대적인 수치가 아니라는 것이다.

레벨이 높아도 허당인 놈들이 있고, 그보다 낮아도 더욱 강한 놈이 있다.

그런 면에서 송일섬은 진짜배기였다. 걸음걸이와 손의 미세한 움직임만 봐도 알 수 있었다. 그가 수많은 실전 경험과 뛰어난 무공을 지닌 검객이라는 것을.

‘저 나이에 저 정도 실력자가 얼마나 있지?’

아무리 명문 대파의 제자가 아니라지만 저 정도 실력이라면 무림에서는 진작 이름이 알려졌어야 했다.

낭중지추(囊中之錐)라는 말이 심심해서 나온 말이 아니니까.

‘그런데 아무도 송곳의 존재를 몰랐단 말이지. 그것도 자그마치 십 년 동안이나.’

결국 답은 하나다.

송곳은 의도적으로 자신을 숨겼다. 제법 오랜 시간을 함께한 용봉표국의 사람들조차 그의 실력을 모를 정도로.

‘이것 봐라…….’

문득 어떤 생각이 뇌리를 스쳤다. 지금으로서는 확신할 수 없지만, 주의 깊게 지켜봐야 할 놈인 건 분명하다.

‘마음 같아서는 지금 당장이라도 나서고 싶지만.’

이건 주화란이 직접 풀어야 하는 매듭이다.

내가 언제든지 출수(出手)할 수 있도록 만반의 준비를 끝마치는 사이, 잠시 주춤했던 허준은 거세게 송일섬을 몰아붙였다.

“송 표두. 아니, 송일섬! 허튼소리는 집어치우고 어서 이실직고하지 못할까!”

“무슨 말을 하는지 모르겠소만.”

“이리 발뺌하니 단도직입적으로 묻지. 천년설삼을 어디에 감추었느냐?”

“모르는 일이오.”

“아직 늦지 않았다. 지금이라도 네 죄를 인정하고 천년설삼의 행방을 털어놓는다면…….”

“모른다 하였소.”

송일섬의 대답에 허준이 착 가라앉은 눈빛으로 그를 응시했다.

“정녕 이렇게 나올 생각이냐?”

“그 말, 그대로 돌려주지.”

“지난 정을 생각해서 마지막 기회를 주었건만…… 어쩔 수 없군.”

허준이 손을 들어 올림과 동시에 이십여 명의 표사들이 앞뒤를 넓게 포위하며 퇴로(退路)를 막았다.

용봉삼표의 남은 두 사람으로 짐작되는 중년 표두들은 허준과 함께 삼각 대형으로 송일섬을 둘러쌌다.

활시위처럼 팽팽한 분위기 속, 침묵을 지키던 주화란이 불쑥 입을 연 것은 바로 그때였다.

“모두 물러서세요.”

“화란아. 순순히 죄를 인정할 놈이 아니다. 우선 제압한 후에…….”

“기다리세요, 허 숙부. 물어볼 것이 있어요.”

쉬리릭!

회전하는 손목, 뱀처럼 휘어진 연검의 검면이 탁자에 쌓인 죽간 중 하나를 쳐 내어 송일섬에게 날려 보냈다.

“이게 무엇이오?”

“흥미로운 기록들이 많더군요.”

죽간에 적힌 내용을 확인한 송일섬이 중얼거렸다.

“이건…….”

“맞아요. 지난 이 년간 송 표두가 책임졌던 표행에 대한 기록입니다.”

“실패한 것들만 모아 놨구려.”

“왜 하오문과 개방이 이런 정보들을 수집했을까요?”

“종남파와 연관이 되어 있다고 생각했겠지.”

“송 표두가 이 년간 맡았던 표행의 횟수는 열다섯 번. 그중 열 번을 실패했고 그때마다 우리 용봉표국은 상당한 위약금을 물어내야 했죠.”

열다섯 번 중에 열 번을 실패하다니. 성공 확률이 절반도 되지 않는다.

저 정도면 개방이나 하오문이 아니라 송일섬의 부모님도 자식을 의심할 거다.

주화란은 담담한 목소리로 말을 이어 갔다.

“그뿐만이 아닙니다. 송 표두가 부장으로 참여한 표행들을 보면 석연치 않은 점들이 참 많더군요.”

“매번 최선을 다했지만 실패했지. 내가 소국주께 드릴 수 있는 대답은 그것밖에 없소.”

“그것으론 부족합니다.”

후웅, 투두둑.

다시 한번 연검이 휘둘러졌고, 검풍(劍風)에 휩쓸린 이십여 개의 죽간은 허공을 가르며 송일섬의 발치 아래 떨어졌다.

“이것들도 전부 나와 연관된 기록이오? 많기도 하군.”

혀를 찬 그가 검을 옆에 기대어 놓고 죽간을 들어 읽기 시작했다.

“저, 저놈이…….”

총표두 허준은 당장이라도 배신자를 향해 달려들고 싶은 마음이 굴뚝같아 보였지만, 주화란의 눈짓에 검을 늘어트려야 했다.

기다림은 그리 길지 않았다.

“그래, 그렇군.”

She had been his sworn brother’s treasured jewel, the one and only niece he had once regarded as more his own child than his biological children.

“H-Hwaran.”

Hope.

*I can survive.*

She was torn between affection and betrayal. That was his only remaining escape.

“I was wrong. It was all my fault!”

“Uncle.”

“Spare me. Please, I’m begging you!”

Heo Jun cried out desperately, heedless of the stunned escorts or the other people watching a trusted superior expose his betrayal.

His dignity? Their contempt?

A dead man could feel neither.

He would do anything if it meant surviving this place and seeing tomorrow’s sun.

“Urgh. Hwaran…”

Heo Jun groaned in pain. Ju Hwaran’s flexible sword had passed straight through his right shoulder, and the hand gripping its hilt trembled faintly.

“Then at least make an excuse. Tell me why you did it. Why you had no other choice.”

If excuses would have raised his chances of survival even slightly, Heo Jun would already have offered every one he could invent.

But he knew Ju Hwaran too well. The fact that she had swung her sword meant she was already certain. A clumsy excuse now would only hasten his death.

He had to beg without reservation and appeal subtly to her emotions.

“It was all this foolish uncle’s fault. I have nothing else to say.”

Heo Jun let his head droop and reddened his eyes.

The effect was immediate. He felt the strength behind her sword weaken and continued.

“I am ashamed to admit that I once accepted a bribe. Then, after my hyung suddenly collapsed, the Zhongnan Sect used it as leverage to approach me, and I… I was afraid I would be cast out. I didn’t want to leave the Escort Bureau I had devoted my entire life to, and I trusted the Zhongnan Sect when they promised they wouldn’t hurt you.”

“…”

“I intended to cooperate only once—just once—but by then, I had already stepped into a swamp I could never escape.”

“Is all of that true?”

“How could I lie to you?”

Despite his claim, Heo Jun’s entire story contained only one truth.

He had accepted a bribe.

He had been the one to approach the Zhongnan Sect after Junzi Sword collapsed, concealing his identity as he did so. Their secret relationship had continued for two years.

*I only have to get through this moment. Just this moment!*

Tears streamed down his face. They held no remorse—only terror of death and a desperate desire to survive.

“Please forgive me…!”

The onlookers shook their heads at his desperate plea. More than a few escorts turned away, unable to bear the sight.

Ju Hwaran did not.

She stared at Heo Jun, biting her lip, then abruptly asked, “How did you steal the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng? I never let it out of my sight for even a moment.”

“Th-that…”

“Tell me the truth.”

The mind-clouding drug was a narcotic that clouded the mind and induced sleep. Its effects had been undeniable.

Even Ju Hwaran, a Peak master, had fallen into a deep sleep, mistaking the drug’s effects for the exhaustion of the journey.

“So that was why you were outside my room that night.”

“I had to conceal my presence even as I left. That bastard—no, Captain Song—remained awake until dawn despite taking the drug.”

Song Ilseom, leaning against the wall with his arms folded, muttered expressionlessly.

“So that was a mind-clouding drug. No wonder I felt unusually tired that day. Use something better next time—assuming you have a next time.”

*What a goddamn bastard.*

Heo Jun barely swallowed the curse rising to his lips and looked at Ju Hwaran.

“Hwangbo Eom, that old man, threatened me. He said that unless I switched the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, he would kill me and my family and wipe out the Yongbong Escort Bureau. I only wanted to protect everyone!”

“Then you made the wrong choice.”

“You’re right. I even went to my hyung’s sickbed once and confessed everything in tears. But… but I couldn’t undo my mistake.”

“Your mistake?”

Ju Hwaran’s eyes trembled at the mention of her father, but only for an instant.

Then she gave a small shake of her head.

“No. You’re wrong. It wasn’t a mistake. It was a choice, Uncle.”

“Hwaran…!”

“My father often told me that every choice carries responsibility. Though he failed to make the family business he inherited prosper, he never once regretted the choices he made.”

Heo Jun suddenly realized that the conflict and uncertainty he had seen in Ju Hwaran’s eyes were fading.

*It can’t be.*

No.

It could not be.

This could not be happening!

Tears and cold sweat streamed down Heo Jun’s cheeks.

He desperately raised his voice.

“Give me one chance! Just one last chance! I’m your father’s one and only sworn younger brother, and your uncle, aren’t I? Hwaran, for the sake of the bond we’ve shared, please!”

“The bond we’ve shared, you say?”

“Yes! I shared thirty years of hardship and joy with my hyung. If your father were here—if it were him—he would not take my life so easily!”

“Uncle Heo. No—Chief Escort Heo Jun.”

Heo Jun stopped pounding his head against the floor and looked up blankly.

His niece’s eyes met his.

They were eyes he had never seen before—cold and utterly devoid of hesitation.

“I am not Junzi Sword Ju Hogun. I am Dagger Hidden Flower Ju Hwaran.”

The next instant, silver sword light filled Heo Jun’s vision.

Swish! Slice!

기다림은 그리 길지 않았다.

주화란이 차갑게 대답했다.

츠츠츠츠!

그녀의 입술 사이로 나직한 목소리가 흘러나왔다.

쐐애애액!

푸푹!

허공을 가르며 빛살처럼 쏘아진 연검이 목표를 정확히 꿰뚫었다.

“화, 화란아.”

“Is this really how you intend to play it?”

“I did my best every time, but I failed. That is the only answer I can give the Young Bureau Head.”

“That isn’t enough.”

“That is truly unfortunate.”

“What is?”

“Though not a single drop of blood connects us, I thought of you as family.”

Thrust!

Thud!

Two birds with one stone.

Song Ilseom would have died branded as a traitor who had betrayed the Yongbong Escort Bureau and colluded with the Zhongnan Sect. The whole matter could have ended quietly, without any further trouble.

*I even hid my identity so thoroughly from the Zhongnan Sect, just in case. How did they figure it out?*

Pain.

A low voice pierced his ears.

“Why did you make that choice, Uncle Heo?”

Heo Jun’s bowed body trembled.

He knew that voice. How could he not?

It belonged to the girl he had watched over since she was a newborn.

She had been his sworn brother’s treasured jewel, the one and only niece he had once regarded as more his own child than his biological children.

And…

She was also the person who had driven a sword through his shoulder.

“H-Hwaran.”

Hope.

She was torn between affection and betrayal. That was his only remaining escape.

“I was wrong. It was all my fault!”

“Uncle.”

“Spare me. Please, I’m begging you!”

His dignity? Their contempt?

A dead man could feel neither.

He would do anything if it meant surviving this place and seeing tomorrow’s sun.

He had to beg without reservation and appeal subtly to her emotions.

I didn’t want to leave the Escort Bureau I had devoted my entire life to, and I trusted the Zhongnan Sect when they promised they wouldn’t hurt you.”

“…”

“I intended to cooperate only once—just once—but by then, I had already stepped into a swamp I could never escape.”

“Is all of that true?”

He had accepted a bribe.

He had been the one to approach the Zhongnan Sect after Junzi Sword collapsed, concealing his identity as he did so. Their secret relationship had continued for two years.

*I only have to get through this moment. Just this moment!*

Tears streamed down his face. They held no remorse—only terror of death and a desperate desire to survive.

“Please forgive me…!”

The onlookers shook their heads at his desperate plea. More than a few escorts turned away, unable to bear the sight.

Ju Hwaran did not.

“Tell me the truth.”

The mind-clouding drug was a narcotic that clouded the mind and induced sleep. Its effects had been undeniable.

Even Ju Hwaran, a Peak master, had fallen into a deep sleep, mistaking the drug’s effects for the exhaustion of the journey.

“So that was why you were outside my room that night.”

“I had to conceal my presence even as I left. That bastard—no, Captain Song—remained awake until dawn despite taking the drug.”

Song Ilseom, leaning against the wall with his arms folded, muttered expressionlessly.

“So that was a mind-clouding drug. No wonder I felt unusually tired that day. Use something better next time—assuming you have a next time.”

*What a goddamn bastard.*

Heo Jun barely swallowed the curse rising to his lips and looked at Ju Hwaran.

“Hwangbo Eom, that old man, threatened me. He said that unless I switched the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, he would kill me and my family and wipe out the Yongbong Escort Bureau. I only wanted to protect everyone!”

“Then you made the wrong choice.”

“You’re right. I even went to my hyung’s sickbed once and confessed everything in tears. But… but I couldn’t undo my mistake.”

“Your mistake?”

Ju Hwaran’s eyes trembled at the mention of her father, but only for an instant.

Then she gave a small shake of her head.

“No. You’re wrong. It wasn’t a mistake. It was a choice, Uncle.”

“Hwaran…!”

“My father often told me that every choice carries responsibility. Though he failed to make the family business he inherited prosper, he never once regretted the choices he made.”

Heo Jun suddenly realized that the conflict and uncertainty he had seen in Ju Hwaran’s eyes were fading.

*It can’t be.*

No.

It could not be.

This could not be happening!

Tears and cold sweat streamed down Heo Jun’s cheeks.

He desperately raised his voice.

“Give me one chance! Just one last chance! I’m your father’s one and only sworn younger brother, and your uncle, aren’t I? Hwaran, for the sake of the bond we’ve shared, please!”

“The bond we’ve shared, you say?”

“Yes! I shared thirty years of hardship and joy with my hyung. If your father were here—if it were him—he would not take my life so easily!”

“Uncle Heo. No—Chief Escort Heo Jun.”

Heo Jun stopped pounding his head against the floor and looked up blankly.

His niece’s eyes met his.

They were eyes he had never seen before—cold and utterly devoid of hesitation.

“You’re right. If my father were here, he would have forgiven you. But…”

Her low voice continued toward the frozen Heo Jun.

“I am not Junzi Sword Ju Hogun. I am Dagger Hidden Flower Ju Hwaran.”

The next instant, silver sword light filled Heo Jun’s vision.

Swish! Slice!

Song Ilseom’s strength.

*He’s quite a master. Stronger than the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.*

Some people had high Levels but were utterly useless, while others were stronger than people above their Level.

*How many people his age are that strong?*

He might not be a disciple of some prestigious sect, but with that much skill, his name should have spread through the Murim long ago.

The saying about a needle in a bag existed for a reason. Exceptional talent was bound to reveal itself eventually.

*Yet no one knew the needle was there. Not for ten whole years.*

There was only one possible answer.

The needle had deliberately kept itself hidden—and done such a thorough job that even the people of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, who had spent years with him, had no idea how strong he truly was.

*Well, well…*

A thought suddenly crossed my mind. I could not be certain yet, but this was clearly someone I needed to watch carefully.

*I’d like to step in right now, but…*

This was a knot Ju Hwaran had to untangle herself.

“I said I don’t know.”

“I gave you one last chance for old times’ sake… but I suppose it can’t be helped.”

The two middle-aged escort captains who appeared to be the other members of the Dragon-Phoenix Three Escorts joined Heo Jun in surrounding Song Ilseom from three sides.

The atmosphere pulled taut as a bowstring.

That was when Ju Hwaran, silent until now, abruptly spoke.

“Everyone, stand back.”

“Wait, Uncle Heo. I have something to ask him.”

Whoosh!

Her wrist turned. The flat of her flexible sword, curving like a snake, struck one of the bamboo slips piled on the table and sent it flying toward Song Ilseom.

“What is this?”

“There are quite a few interesting records here.”

Song Ilseom checked what was written on the bamboo slip and muttered.

“This is…”

“That’s right. Records of the escort missions you were responsible for over the past two years.”

“You’ve collected only the failures.”

“Why do you think the Lower District Sect and the Beggars’ Sect gathered this information?”

“They must have suspected a connection to the Zhongnan Sect.”

“You were responsible for fifteen escort missions over the past two years. Ten of them failed, and every failure forced the Yongbong Escort Bureau to pay a substantial contractual penalty.”

Ten failures out of fifteen. His success rate was below fifty percent.

At that point, even Song Ilseom’s parents would have suspected him, never mind the Beggars’ Sect or the Lower District Sect.

Ju Hwaran continued calmly.

“That isn’t all. The missions on which you served as assistant escort captain contain a remarkable number of suspicious details.”

“I did my best every time, but I failed. That is the only answer I can give the Young Bureau Head.”

“That isn’t enough.”

Whoosh! Clatter!

The flexible sword swept out again. More than twenty bamboo slips caught in its sword wind, sailed through the air, and scattered at Song Ilseom’s feet.

“Are these all records connected to me? There certainly are a lot.”

Clicking his tongue, he propped his sword beside him and began picking up the bamboo slips one by one to read.

“That bastard…”

Chief Escort Heo Jun looked ready to charge at the traitor then and there, but at a glance from Ju Hwaran, he had no choice but to let his sword droop.

They did not have to wait long.

“So that’s how it was.”

Song Ilseom set down the final bamboo slip and arched his fierce eyebrows.

“How did you know?”

“You were clever. Clever enough that each incident could be dismissed as a simple mistake.”

“You figured it out from this alone? You’re sharper than I expected. I thought you were merely a child, but… I underestimated you.”

“That is truly unfortunate.”

“What is?”

“Though not a single drop of blood connects us, I thought of you as family.”

“Family? What weak-minded nonsense. Time changes even mountains and rivers. How could people be any different?”

At some point, Song Ilseom had gone from formal courtesy to openly talking down to her. Yet somehow, the change felt as natural as flowing water.

Like a man finally shedding a stifling set of clothes, he asked with an air of relief, “So what will you do now?”

“Punish the criminal.”

“Children resemble their parents. But can the daughter of Junzi Sword[^1] truly do it?”

Ju Hwaran answered coldly.

“It is something I have to do, and I will do it.”

Hissssss!

Her flexible sword, charged with internal energy, rose stiffly into the air. Ju Hwaran’s hardened face was reflected in the transparent blade.

Her voice came low.

“No matter who it may be.”

Whoosh!

She moved without warning, faster than anyone else in the Yongbong Escort Bureau.

Ju Hwaran might have only just entered the Peak realm, but she was still a Peak master. The essence of speed permeated both her sword arts and her movement technique.

Thrust!

The flexible sword streaked through the air like a ray of light and pierced its target precisely.

A wet sound rang out as it pierced flesh. Blood spurted into the air, followed by a scream from a single man.

“Gaaah!”

Ju Hwaran’s eyelids trembled as she watched him sink to his knees, scattering blood.

What followed was a question for one man.

A condemnation of the person she had never once doubted.

“Why did you make that choice, Uncle Heo?”

“H-Hwaran.”

The man raised his head.

Chief Escort Heo Jun’s face was deathly pale.

* * *

Whoosh!

Heo Jun’s hair stood on end, and a chill ran down his spine. But by the time he registered the faint sound of something cutting through the air, it was already too late.

Thud!

The blade piercing his flesh was cold as ice. The pain that followed burned like fire.

Chief Escort Heo Jun dropped to his knees with a scream.

Even then, only one thought circled through his blank, bleached-white mind.

*It’s all gone wrong.*

The unexpected appearance of Jin Taekyung had overturned the entire situation, but that had not necessarily been bad for Heo Jun.

Over the past two years, he had secretly skimmed off several thousand silver nyang[^2] by disguising his thefts as mistakes—sometimes small, sometimes audacious.

He had already amassed an enormous fortune. If this incident led to the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s revival, his authority as Chief Escort would only grow.

Best of all, he could escape the guilt of betraying those who trusted him.

Two birds with one stone.

But then…

*Why now, of all times?!*

If he cut Song Ilseom’s throat, everything would be over.

Song Ilseom would have died branded as a traitor who had betrayed the Yongbong Escort Bureau and colluded with the Zhongnan Sect. The whole matter could have ended quietly, without any further trouble.

*I even hid my identity so thoroughly from the Zhongnan Sect, just in case. How did they figure it out?*

Pain.

And shock even greater than the pain froze Heo Jun where he knelt.

A low voice pierced his ears.

“Why did you make that choice, Uncle Heo?”

Heo Jun’s bowed body trembled.

He knew that voice. How could he not?

It belonged to the girl he had watched over since she was a newborn.

She had been his sworn brother’s treasured jewel, the one and only niece he had once regarded as more his own child than his biological children.

And…

She was also the person who had driven a sword through his shoulder.

“H-Hwaran.”

Heo Jun slowly raised his head and met Ju Hwaran’s downward gaze.

Unlike her calm voice, her eyes trembled with emotion. At the sight of them, a feeling he had momentarily forgotten reared its head.

Hope.

*I can survive.*

Heo Jun recognized the turmoil in Ju Hwaran’s eyes at once.

She was torn between affection and betrayal. That was his only remaining escape.

“I was wrong. It was all my fault!”

“Uncle.”

“Spare me. Please, I’m begging you!”

Heo Jun cried out desperately, heedless of the stunned escorts or the other people watching a trusted superior expose his betrayal.

His dignity? Their contempt?

A dead man could feel neither.

He would do anything if it meant surviving this place and seeing tomorrow’s sun.

“Urgh. Hwaran…”

Heo Jun groaned in pain. Ju Hwaran’s flexible sword had passed straight through his right shoulder, and the hand gripping its hilt trembled faintly.

“Then at least make an excuse. Tell me why you did it. Why you had no other choice.”

If excuses would have raised his chances of survival even slightly, Heo Jun would already have offered every one he could invent.

But he knew Ju Hwaran too well. The fact that she had swung her sword meant she was already certain. A clumsy excuse now would only hasten his death.

He had to beg without reservation and appeal subtly to her emotions.

“It was all this foolish uncle’s fault. I have nothing else to say.”

Heo Jun let his head droop and reddened his eyes.

The effect was immediate. He felt the strength behind her sword weaken and continued.

“I am ashamed to admit that I once accepted a bribe. Then, after my hyung[^3] suddenly collapsed, the Zhongnan Sect used it as leverage to approach me, and I… I was afraid I would be cast out. I didn’t want to leave the Escort Bureau I had devoted my entire life to, and I trusted the Zhongnan Sect when they promised they wouldn’t hurt you.”

“…”

“I intended to cooperate only once—just once—but by then, I had already stepped into a swamp I could never escape.”

“Is all of that true?”

“How could I lie to you?”

Despite his claim, Heo Jun’s entire story contained only one truth.

He had accepted a bribe.

He had been the one to approach the Zhongnan Sect after Junzi Sword collapsed, concealing his identity as he did so. Their secret relationship had continued for two years.

*I only have to get through this moment. Just this moment!*

Tears streamed down his face. They held no remorse—only terror of death and a desperate desire to survive.

“Please forgive me…!”

The onlookers shook their heads at his desperate plea. More than a few escorts turned away, unable to bear the sight.

Ju Hwaran did not.

She stared at Heo Jun, biting her lip, then abruptly asked, “How did you steal the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng? I never let it out of my sight for even a moment.”

“Th-that…”

“Tell me the truth.”

“…I mixed a mind-clouding drug into the food. Everyone was exhausted, so a small dose was enough.”

The mind-clouding drug was a narcotic that clouded the mind and induced sleep. Its effects had been undeniable.

Even Ju Hwaran, a Peak master, had fallen into a deep sleep, mistaking the drug’s effects for the exhaustion of the journey.

“So that was why you were outside my room that night.”

“I had to conceal my presence even as I left. That bastard—no, Captain Song—remained awake until dawn despite taking the drug.”

Song Ilseom, leaning against the wall with his arms folded, muttered expressionlessly.

“So that was a mind-clouding drug. No wonder I felt unusually tired that day. Use something better next time—assuming you have a next time.”

*What a goddamn bastard.*

Heo Jun barely swallowed the curse rising to his lips and looked at Ju Hwaran.

“Hwangbo Eom, that old man, threatened me. He said that unless I switched the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, he would kill me and my family and wipe out the Yongbong Escort Bureau. I only wanted to protect everyone!”

“Then you made the wrong choice.”

“You’re right. I even went to my hyung’s[^3] sickbed once and confessed everything in tears. But… but I couldn’t undo my mistake.”

“Your mistake?”

Ju Hwaran’s eyes trembled at the mention of her father, but only for an instant.

Then she gave a small shake of her head.

“No. You’re wrong. It wasn’t a mistake. It was a choice, Uncle.”

“Hwaran…!”

“My father often told me that every choice carries responsibility. Though he failed to make the family business he inherited prosper, he never once regretted the choices he made.”

Heo Jun suddenly realized that the conflict and uncertainty he had seen in Ju Hwaran’s eyes were fading.

*It can’t be.*

No.

It could not be.

This could not be happening!

Tears and cold sweat streamed down Heo Jun’s cheeks.

He desperately raised his voice.

“Give me one chance! Just one last chance! I’m your father’s one and only sworn younger brother, and your uncle, aren’t I? Hwaran, for the sake of the bond we’ve shared, please!”

“The bond we’ve shared, you say?”

“Yes! I shared thirty years of hardship and joy with my hyung.[^3] If your father were here—if it were him—he would not take my life so easily!”

“Uncle Heo. No—Chief Escort Heo Jun.”

Heo Jun stopped pounding his head against the floor and looked up blankly.

His niece’s eyes met his.

They were eyes he had never seen before—cold and utterly devoid of hesitation.

“You’re right. If my father were here, he would have forgiven you. But…”

Her low voice continued toward the frozen Heo Jun.

“I am not Junzi Sword Ju Hogun. I am Dagger Hidden Flower Ju Hwaran.”

The next instant, silver sword light filled Heo Jun’s vision.

Swish! Slice!

[^1]: *Junzi* is the Confucian ideal of a morally upright gentleman.
[^2]: A *nyang* is a traditional unit of currency; here, the amount is denominated in silver.
[^3]: *Hyung* is a Korean term a man uses for an older brother or a close older man. Heo Jun uses it for his sworn brother, Ju Hogun.

결국 답은 하나다.

송일섬의 대답에 허준이 착 가라앉은 눈빛으로 그를 응시했다.

용봉삼표의 남은 두 사람으로 짐작되는 중년 표두들은 허준과 함께 삼각 대형으로 송일섬을 둘러쌌다.

쉬리릭!

회전하는 손목, 뱀처럼 휘어진 연검의 검면이 탁자에 쌓인 죽간 중 하나를 쳐 내어 송일섬에게 날려 보냈다.

“이게 무엇이오?”

죽간에 적힌 내용을 확인한 송일섬이 중얼거렸다.

“이건…….”

“실패한 것들만 모아 놨구려.”

후웅, 투두둑.

“이것들도 전부 나와 연관된 기록이오? 많기도 하군.”

혀를 찬 그가 검을 옆에 기대어 놓고 죽간을 들어 읽기 시작했다.

“저, 저놈이…….”

총표두 허준은 당장이라도 배신자를 향해 달려들고 싶은 마음이 굴뚝같아 보였지만, 주화란의 눈짓에 검을 늘어트려야 했다.

기다림은 그리 길지 않았다.

“그래, 그렇군.”

중얼거림과 함께 마지막 죽간을 내려놓은 송일섬이 사나워 보이는 눈썹을 치켜떴다.

“어떻게 알았지?”

“교묘하더군요. 실수로 눈감고 넘어가 줄 수 있을 만큼.”

“이것만으로도 파악하다니, 생각했던 것 이상으로 명석하군. 그저 어린애라고만 생각했는데…… 내 너를 과소평가했다.”

“참으로 애석하네요.”

“뭐가 말이냐?”

“비록 피 한 방울 섞이지 않았지만, 가족이라 생각했으니까.”

“가족이라. 유약한 소리다. 세월은 강산(江山)도 바꾸는데, 사람은 오죽할까.”

어느새 송일섬의 말투는 하오체에서 완전한 하대로 바뀌어 있었다. 하지만 왠지 모르게 그 모든 것들이 흐르는 물처럼 자연스러웠다.

“자, 그래서 이제 어쩔 셈이지?”

“죄인을 벌해야지요.”

“자식은 부모를 닮는 법. 군자검의 핏줄인 네가 할 수 있을까.”

주화란이 차갑게 대답했다.

“해야 하는 일이고, 해낼 겁니다.”

츠츠츠츠!

공력이 실린 연검이 빳빳하게 솟구친다. 투명한 검신에 주화란의 굳은 얼굴이 비쳤다.

그녀의 입술 사이로 나직한 목소리가 흘러나왔다.

“상대가 그 누구라 할지라도.”

쐐애애액!

아무런 예고도 없이 움직인 그녀는 용봉표국의 누구보다 빨랐다.

아직 초입에 불과하나 주화란 역시 한 사람의 절정 고수. 검공과 신법에는 쾌(快)의 묘리가 스며들어 있었다.

푸푹!

허공을 가르며 빛살처럼 쏘아진 연검이 목표를 정확히 꿰뚫었다.

“크아아악!”

피를 흩뿌리며 무릎 꿇는 사내를 바라보는 주화란의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.

“왜 그런 선택을 하신 겁니까, 허 숙부.”

“화, 화란아.”

“내가 잘못했다. 전부 내 잘못이다!”

“We still have the most important matter left to discuss. Don’t you agree?”

Ju Hwaran stood with her sword lowered at her side, beautiful and cold.

A frost-sharp aura surged around her, directed at one person.

“Captain Song.”

Everyone followed Ju Hwaran’s gaze. At its end stood a man who appeared to be in his early thirties. He was fairly handsome, save for the fierce upward slant of his eyebrows.

Song Ilseom’s lips twisted, and a chilly voice emerged.

“Th-that’s…”

“You needn’t answer. I don’t care what you call the Young Bureau Head. Just don’t demand courtesy from me.”

His tone and behavior were obnoxious, but Song Ilseom did have a point.

As I watched Heo Jun struggle for words, Wolhwa whispered to me.

“Young Master Jin, do you know that man well?”

“Who? Heo Jun? Or…”

“The young, handsome one, obviously. I already know who Chief Escort Heo is.”

“Then why are you asking me? You’re the Shaanxi Branch Leader of the Lower District Sect, of all people.”

“It’s nice that you think so highly of me, but what could a Branch Leader who’s been at her post for less than half a year possibly know? A disciple from a famous major sect would be one thing, but even I can’t keep track of every ordinary escort.”

“An ordinary escort… Do you know who he is?”

“Hmm. I know that one of the Dragon-Phoenix Three Escorts is young and has a nasty temper. That’s about it.”

Song Ilseom. Position: escort captain.

That was about all I knew of him too.

But I knew one thing Wolhwa did not.

Song Ilseom’s strength.

*He’s quite a master. Stronger than the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.*

If there was one thing I had learned from going back and forth between the Murim and the modern world, it was that Level was never an absolute measure.

Some people had high Levels but were utterly useless, while others were stronger than people above their Level.

Song Ilseom was the real deal. I could tell just from his gait and the minute movements of his hands. He was a swordsman with extensive combat experience and exceptional martial arts.

*How many people his age are that strong?*

He might not be a disciple of some prestigious sect, but with that much skill, his name should have spread through the Murim long ago.

The saying about a needle in a bag existed for a reason. Exceptional talent was bound to reveal itself eventually.

*Yet no one knew the needle was there. Not for ten whole years.*

There was only one possible answer.

The needle had deliberately kept itself hidden—and done such a thorough job that even the people of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, who had spent years with him, had no idea how strong he truly was.

*Well, well…*

A thought suddenly crossed my mind. I could not be certain yet, but this was clearly someone I needed to watch carefully.

*I’d like to step in right now, but…*

This was a knot Ju Hwaran had to untangle herself.

While I finished preparing to intervene at any moment, Heo Jun recovered from his hesitation and pressed Song Ilseom even harder.

“Captain Song. No, Song Ilseom! Enough nonsense. Confess everything!”

“I don’t know what you’re talking about.”

“Fine. I’ll ask you directly. Where did you hide the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng?”

“I know nothing about it.”

“It’s not too late. If you admit your crimes and tell us where the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng is, even now…”

“I said I don’t know.”

At Song Ilseom’s answer, Heo Jun stared at him with eyes that had gone flat and cold.

“Is this really how you intend to play it?”

“I could say the same to you.”

“I gave you one last chance for old times’ sake… but I suppose it can’t be helped.”

Heo Jun raised his hand. More than twenty escorts spread out around Song Ilseom, sealing off every escape route.

The two middle-aged escort captains who appeared to be the other members of the Dragon-Phoenix Three Escorts joined Heo Jun in surrounding Song Ilseom from three sides.

The atmosphere pulled taut as a bowstring.

That was when Ju Hwaran, silent until now, abruptly spoke.

“Everyone, stand back.”

“Hwaran, he won’t confess willingly. We should subdue him first, then—”

“Wait, Uncle Heo. I have something to ask him.”

Whoosh!

Her wrist turned. The flat of her flexible sword, curving like a snake, struck one of the bamboo slips piled on the table and sent it flying toward Song Ilseom.

“What is this?”

“There are quite a few interesting records here.”

Song Ilseom checked what was written on the bamboo slip and muttered.

“This is…”

“That’s right. Records of the escort missions you were responsible for over the past two years.”

“You’ve collected only the failures.”

“Why do you think the Lower District Sect and the Beggars’ Sect gathered this information?”

“They must have suspected a connection to the Zhongnan Sect.”

“You were responsible for fifteen escort missions over the past two years. Ten of them failed, and every failure forced the Yongbong Escort Bureau to pay a substantial contractual penalty.”

Ten failures out of fifteen. His success rate was below fifty percent.

At that point, even Song Ilseom’s parents would have suspected him, never mind the Beggars’ Sect or the Lower District Sect.

Ju Hwaran continued calmly.

“That isn’t all. The missions on which you served as assistant escort captain contain a remarkable number of suspicious details.”

“I did my best every time, but I failed. That is the only answer I can give the Young Bureau Head.”

“That isn’t enough.”

Whoosh! Clatter!

The flexible sword swept out again. More than twenty bamboo slips caught in its sword wind, sailed through the air, and scattered at Song Ilseom’s feet.

“Are these all records connected to me? There certainly are a lot.”

Clicking his tongue, he propped his sword beside him and began picking up the bamboo slips one by one to read.

“That bastard…”

Chief Escort Heo Jun looked ready to charge at the traitor then and there, but at a glance from Ju Hwaran, he had no choice but to let his sword droop.

They did not have to wait long.

“So that’s how it was.”

Song Ilseom set down the final bamboo slip and arched his fierce eyebrows.

“How did you know?”

“You were clever. Clever enough that each incident could be dismissed as a simple mistake.”

“You figured it out from this alone? You’re sharper than I expected. I thought you were merely a child, but… I underestimated you.”

“That is truly unfortunate.”

“What is?”

“Though not a single drop of blood connects us, I thought of you as family.”

“Family? What weak-minded nonsense. Time changes even mountains and rivers. How could people be any different?”

At some point, Song Ilseom had gone from formal courtesy to openly talking down to her. Yet somehow, the change felt as natural as flowing water.

Like a man finally shedding a stifling set of clothes, he asked with an air of relief, “So what will you do now?”

“Punish the criminal.”

“Children resemble their parents. But can the daughter of Junzi Sword truly do it?”

Ju Hwaran answered coldly.

“It is something I have to do, and I will do it.”

Hissssss!

Her flexible sword, charged with internal energy, rose stiffly into the air. Ju Hwaran’s hardened face was reflected in the transparent blade.

Her voice came low.

“No matter who it may be.”

Whoosh!

She moved without warning, faster than anyone else in the Yongbong Escort Bureau.

Ju Hwaran might have only just entered the Peak realm, but she was still a Peak master. The essence of speed permeated both her sword arts and her movement technique.

Thrust!

The flexible sword streaked through the air like a ray of light and pierced its target precisely.

A wet sound rang out as it pierced flesh. Blood spurted into the air, followed by a scream from a single man.

“Gaaah!”

Ju Hwaran’s eyelids trembled as she watched him sink to his knees, scattering blood.

What followed was a question for one man.

A condemnation of the person she had never once doubted.

“Why did you make that choice, Uncle Heo?”

“H-Hwaran.”

The man raised his head.

Chief Escort Heo Jun’s face was deathly pale.

* * *

Whoosh!

Heo Jun’s hair stood on end, and a chill ran down his spine. But by the time he registered the faint sound of something cutting through the air, it was already too late.

Thud!

The blade piercing his flesh was cold as ice. The pain that followed burned like fire.

Chief Escort Heo Jun dropped to his knees with a scream.

Even then, only one thought circled through his blank, bleached-white mind.

*It’s all gone wrong.*

The unexpected appearance of Jin Taekyung had overturned the entire situation, but that had not necessarily been bad for Heo Jun.

Over the past two years, he had secretly skimmed off several thousand silver nyang by disguising his thefts as mistakes—sometimes small, sometimes audacious.

He had already amassed an enormous fortune. If this incident led to the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s revival, his authority as Chief Escort would only grow.

Best of all, he could escape the guilt of betraying those who trusted him.

Two birds with one stone.

But then…

*Why now, of all times?!*

If he cut Song Ilseom’s throat, everything would be over.

Song Ilseom would have died branded as a traitor who had betrayed the Yongbong Escort Bureau and colluded with the Zhongnan Sect. The whole matter could have ended quietly, without any further trouble.

*I even hid my identity so thoroughly from the Zhongnan Sect, just in case. How did they figure it out?*

Pain.

And shock even greater than the pain froze Heo Jun where he knelt.

A low voice pierced his ears.

“Why did you make that choice, Uncle Heo?”

Heo Jun’s bowed body trembled.

He knew that voice. How could he not?

It belonged to the girl he had watched over since she was a newborn.

She had been his sworn brother’s treasured jewel, the one and only niece he had once regarded as more his own child than his biological children.

And…

She was also the person who had driven a sword through his shoulder.

“H-Hwaran.”

Heo Jun slowly raised his head and met Ju Hwaran’s downward gaze.

Unlike her calm voice, her eyes trembled with emotion. At the sight of them, a feeling he had momentarily forgotten reared its head.

Hope.

*I can survive.*

Heo Jun recognized the turmoil in Ju Hwaran’s eyes at once.

She was torn between affection and betrayal. That was his only remaining escape.

“I was wrong. It was all my fault!”

“Uncle.”

“Spare me. Please, I’m begging you!”

Heo Jun cried out desperately, heedless of the stunned escorts or the other people watching a trusted superior expose his betrayal.

His dignity? Their contempt?

A dead man could feel neither.

He would do anything if it meant surviving this place and seeing tomorrow’s sun.

“Urgh. Hwaran…”

Heo Jun groaned in pain. Ju Hwaran’s flexible sword had passed straight through his right shoulder, and the hand gripping its hilt trembled faintly.

“Then at least make an excuse. Tell me why you did it. Why you had no other choice.”

If excuses would have raised his chances of survival even slightly, Heo Jun would already have offered every one he could invent.

But he knew Ju Hwaran too well. The fact that she had swung her sword meant she was already certain. A clumsy excuse now would only hasten his death.

He had to beg without reservation and appeal subtly to her emotions.

“It was all this foolish uncle’s fault. I have nothing else to say.”

Heo Jun let his head droop and reddened his eyes.

The effect was immediate. He felt the strength behind her sword weaken and continued.

“I am ashamed to admit that I once accepted a bribe. Then, after my hyung suddenly collapsed, the Zhongnan Sect used it as leverage to approach me, and I… I was afraid I would be cast out. I didn’t want to leave the Escort Bureau I had devoted my entire life to, and I trusted the Zhongnan Sect when they promised they wouldn’t hurt you.”

“…”

“I intended to cooperate only once—just once—but by then, I had already stepped into a swamp I could never escape.”

“Is all of that true?”

“How could I lie to you?”

Despite his claim, Heo Jun’s entire story contained only one truth.

He had accepted a bribe.

He had been the one to approach the Zhongnan Sect after Junzi Sword collapsed, concealing his identity as he did so. Their secret relationship had continued for two years.

*I only have to get through this moment. Just this moment!*

Tears streamed down his face. They held no remorse—only terror of death and a desperate desire to survive.

“Please forgive me…!”

The onlookers shook their heads at his desperate plea. More than a few escorts turned away, unable to bear the sight.

Ju Hwaran did not.

She stared at Heo Jun, biting her lip, then abruptly asked, “How did you steal the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng? I never let it out of my sight for even a moment.”

“Th-that…”

“Tell me the truth.”

“…I mixed a mind-clouding drug into the food. Everyone was exhausted, so a small dose was enough.”

The mind-clouding drug was a narcotic that clouded the mind and induced sleep. Its effects had been undeniable.

Even Ju Hwaran, a Peak master, had fallen into a deep sleep, mistaking the drug’s effects for the exhaustion of the journey.

“So that was why you were outside my room that night.”

“I had to conceal my presence even as I left. That bastard—no, Captain Song—remained awake until dawn despite taking the drug.”

Song Ilseom, leaning against the wall with his arms folded, muttered expressionlessly.

“So that was a mind-clouding drug. No wonder I felt unusually tired that day. Use something better next time—assuming you have a next time.”

*What a goddamn bastard.*

Heo Jun barely swallowed the curse rising to his lips and looked at Ju Hwaran.

“Hwangbo Eom, that old man, threatened me. He said that unless I switched the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, he would kill me and my family and wipe out the Yongbong Escort Bureau. I only wanted to protect everyone!”

“Then you made the wrong choice.”

“You’re right. I even went to my hyung’s sickbed once and confessed everything in tears. But… but I couldn’t undo my mistake.”

“Your mistake?”

Ju Hwaran’s eyes trembled at the mention of her father, but only for an instant.

Then she gave a small shake of her head.

“No. You’re wrong. It wasn’t a mistake. It was a choice, Uncle.”

“Hwaran…!”

“My father often told me that every choice carries responsibility. Though he failed to make the family business he inherited prosper, he never once regretted the choices he made.”

Heo Jun suddenly realized that the conflict and uncertainty he had seen in Ju Hwaran’s eyes were fading.

*It can’t be.*

No.

It could not be.

This could not be happening!

Tears and cold sweat streamed down Heo Jun’s cheeks.

He desperately raised his voice.

“Give me one chance! Just one last chance! I’m your father’s one and only sworn younger brother, and your uncle, aren’t I? Hwaran, for the sake of the bond we’ve shared, please!”

“The bond we’ve shared, you say?”

“Yes! I shared thirty years of hardship and joy with my hyung. If your father were here—if it were him—he would not take my life so easily!”

“Uncle Heo. No—Chief Escort Heo Jun.”

Heo Jun stopped pounding his head against the floor and looked up blankly.

His niece’s eyes met his.

They were eyes he had never seen before—cold and utterly devoid of hesitation.

“You’re right. If my father were here, he would have forgiven you. But…”

Her low voice continued toward the frozen Heo Jun.

“I am not Junzi Sword Ju Hogun. I am Dagger Hidden Flower Ju Hwaran.”

The next instant, silver sword light filled Heo Jun’s vision.

Swish! Slice!

The saying about a needle in a bag existed for a reason. Exceptional talent was bound to reveal itself eventually.

*Yet no one knew the needle was there. Not for ten whole years.*

There was only one possible answer.

The needle had deliberately kept itself hidden—and done such a thorough job that even the people of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, who had spent years with him, had no idea how strong he truly was.

*Well, well…*

A thought suddenly crossed my mind. I could not be certain yet, but this was clearly someone I needed to watch carefully.

*I’d like to step in right now, but…*

This was a knot Ju Hwaran had to untangle herself.

While I finished preparing to intervene at any moment, Heo Jun recovered from his hesitation and pressed Song Ilseom even harder.

“Captain Song. No, Song Ilseom! Enough nonsense. Confess everything!”

“I don’t know what you’re talking about.”

“Fine. I’ll ask you directly. Where did you hide the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng?”

“I know nothing about it.”

“It’s not too late. If you admit your crimes and tell us where the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng is, even now…”

“I said I don’t know.”

At Song Ilseom’s answer, Heo Jun stared at him with eyes that had gone flat and cold.

“Is this really how you intend to play it?”

“I could say the same to you.”

“I gave you one last chance for old times’ sake… but I suppose it can’t be helped.”

Heo Jun raised his hand. More than twenty escorts spread out around Song Ilseom, sealing off every escape route.

The two middle-aged escort captains who appeared to be the other members of the Dragon-Phoenix Three Escorts joined Heo Jun in surrounding Song Ilseom from three sides.

The atmosphere pulled taut as a bowstring.

That was when Ju Hwaran, silent until now, abruptly spoke.

“Everyone, stand back.”

“Hwaran, he won’t confess willingly. We should subdue him first, then—”

“Wait, Uncle Heo. I have something to ask him.”

Whoosh!

Her wrist turned. The flat of her flexible sword, curving like a snake, struck one of the bamboo slips piled on the table and sent it flying toward Song Ilseom.

“What is this?”

“There are quite a few interesting records here.”

Song Ilseom checked what was written on the bamboo slip and muttered.

“This is…”

“That’s right. Records of the escort missions you were responsible for over the past two years.”

“You’ve collected only the failures.”

“Why do you think the Lower District Sect and the Beggars’ Sect gathered this information?”

“They must have suspected a connection to the Zhongnan Sect.”

“You were responsible for fifteen escort missions over the past two years. Ten of them failed, and every failure forced the Yongbong Escort Bureau to pay a substantial contractual penalty.”

Ten failures out of fifteen. His success rate was below fifty percent.

At that point, even Song Ilseom’s parents would have suspected him, never mind the Beggars’ Sect or the Lower District Sect.

Ju Hwaran continued calmly.

“That isn’t all. The missions on which you served as assistant escort captain contain a remarkable number of suspicious details.”

“I did my best every time, but I failed. That is the only answer I can give the Young Bureau Head.”

“That isn’t enough.”

Whoosh! Clatter!

The flexible sword swept out again. More than twenty bamboo slips caught in its sword wind, sailed through the air, and scattered at Song Ilseom’s feet.

“Are these all records connected to me? There certainly are a lot.”

Clicking his tongue, he propped his sword beside him and began picking up the bamboo slips one by one to read.

“That bastard…”

Chief Escort Heo Jun looked ready to charge at the traitor then and there, but at a glance from Ju Hwaran, he had no choice but to let his sword droop.

They did not have to wait long.

“So that’s how it was.”

Song Ilseom set down the final bamboo slip and arched his fierce eyebrows.

“How did you know?”

“You were clever. Clever enough that each incident could be dismissed as a simple mistake.”

“You figured it out from this alone? You’re sharper than I expected. I thought you were merely a child, but… I underestimated you.”

“That is truly unfortunate.”

“What is?”

“Though not a single drop of blood connects us, I thought of you as family.”

“Family? What weak-minded nonsense. Time changes even mountains and rivers. How could people be any different?”

At some point, Song Ilseom had gone from formal courtesy to openly talking down to her. Yet somehow, the change felt as natural as flowing water.

Like a man finally shedding a stifling set of clothes, he asked with an air of relief, “So what will you do now?”

“Punish the criminal.”

“Children resemble their parents. But can the daughter of Junzi Sword[^1] truly do it?”

Ju Hwaran answered coldly.

“It is something I have to do, and I will do it.”

Hissssss!

Her flexible sword, charged with internal energy, rose stiffly into the air. Ju Hwaran’s hardened face was reflected in the transparent blade.

Her voice came low.

“No matter who it may be.”

Whoosh!

She moved without warning, faster than anyone else in the Yongbong Escort Bureau.

Ju Hwaran might have only just entered the Peak realm, but she was still a Peak master. The essence of speed permeated both her sword arts and her movement technique.

Thrust!

The flexible sword streaked through the air like a ray of light and pierced its target precisely.

A wet sound rang out as it pierced flesh. Blood spurted into the air, followed by a scream from a single man.

“Gaaah!”

Ju Hwaran’s eyelids trembled as she watched him sink to his knees, scattering blood.

What followed was a question for one man.

A condemnation of the person she had never once doubted.

“Why did you make that choice, Uncle Heo?”

“H-Hwaran.”

The man raised his head.

Chief Escort Heo Jun’s face was deathly pale.

* * *

Whoosh!

Heo Jun’s hair stood on end, and a chill ran down his spine. But by the time he registered the faint sound of something cutting through the air, it was already too late.

Thud!

The blade piercing his flesh was cold as ice. The pain that followed burned like fire.

Chief Escort Heo Jun dropped to his knees with a scream.

Even then, only one thought circled through his blank, bleached-white mind.

*It’s all gone wrong.*

The unexpected appearance of Jin Taekyung had overturned the entire situation, but that had not necessarily been bad for Heo Jun.

Over the past two years, he had secretly skimmed off several thousand silver nyang[^2] by disguising his thefts as mistakes—sometimes small, sometimes audacious.

He had already amassed an enormous fortune. If this incident led to the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s revival, his authority as Chief Escort would only grow.

Best of all, he could escape the guilt of betraying those who trusted him.

Two birds with one stone.

But then…

*Why now, of all times?!*

If he cut Song Ilseom’s throat, everything would be over.

Song Ilseom would have died branded as a traitor who had betrayed the Yongbong Escort Bureau and colluded with the Zhongnan Sect. The whole matter could have ended quietly, without any further trouble.

*I even hid my identity so thoroughly from the Zhongnan Sect, just in case. How did they figure it out?*

Pain.

And shock even greater than the pain froze Heo Jun where he knelt.

A low voice pierced his ears.

“Why did you make that choice, Uncle Heo?”

Heo Jun’s bowed body trembled.

He knew that voice. How could he not?

It belonged to the girl he had watched over since she was a newborn.

She had been his sworn brother’s treasured jewel, the one and only niece he had once regarded as more his own child than his biological children.

And…

She was also the person who had driven a sword through his shoulder.

“H-Hwaran.”

Heo Jun slowly raised his head and met Ju Hwaran’s downward gaze.

Unlike her calm voice, her eyes trembled with emotion. At the sight of them, a feeling he had momentarily forgotten reared its head.

Hope.

*I can survive.*

Heo Jun recognized the turmoil in Ju Hwaran’s eyes at once.

She was torn between affection and betrayal. That was his only remaining escape.

“I was wrong. It was all my fault!”

“Uncle.”

“Spare me. Please, I’m begging you!”

Heo Jun cried out desperately, heedless of the stunned escorts or the other people watching a trusted superior expose his betrayal.

His dignity? Their contempt?

A dead man could feel neither.

He would do anything if it meant surviving this place and seeing tomorrow’s sun.

“Urgh. Hwaran…”

Heo Jun groaned in pain. Ju Hwaran’s flexible sword had passed straight through his right shoulder, and the hand gripping its hilt trembled faintly.

“Then at least make an excuse. Tell me why you did it. Why you had no other choice.”

If excuses would have raised his chances of survival even slightly, Heo Jun would already have offered every one he could invent.

But he knew Ju Hwaran too well. The fact that she had swung her sword meant she was already certain. A clumsy excuse now would only hasten his death.

He had to beg without reservation and appeal subtly to her emotions.

“It was all this foolish uncle’s fault. I have nothing else to say.”

Heo Jun let his head droop and reddened his eyes.

The effect was immediate. He felt the strength behind her sword weaken and continued.

“I am ashamed to admit that I once accepted a bribe. Then, after my hyung[^3] suddenly collapsed, the Zhongnan Sect used it as leverage to approach me, and I… I was afraid I would be cast out. I didn’t want to leave the Escort Bureau I had devoted my entire life to, and I trusted the Zhongnan Sect when they promised they wouldn’t hurt you.”

“…”

“I intended to cooperate only once—just once—but by then, I had already stepped into a swamp I could never escape.”

“Is all of that true?”

“How could I lie to you?”

Despite his claim, Heo Jun’s entire story contained only one truth.

He had accepted a bribe.

He had been the one to approach the Zhongnan Sect after Junzi Sword collapsed, concealing his identity as he did so. Their secret relationship had continued for two years.

*I only have to get through this moment. Just this moment!*

Tears streamed down his face. They held no remorse—only terror of death and a desperate desire to survive.

“Please forgive me…!”

The onlookers shook their heads at his desperate plea. More than a few escorts turned away, unable to bear the sight.

Ju Hwaran did not.

She stared at Heo Jun, biting her lip, then abruptly asked, “How did you steal the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng? I never let it out of my sight for even a moment.”

“Th-that…”

“Tell me the truth.”

“…I mixed a mind-clouding drug into the food. Everyone was exhausted, so a small dose was enough.”

The mind-clouding drug was a narcotic that clouded the mind and induced sleep. Its effects had been undeniable.

Even Ju Hwaran, a Peak master, had fallen into a deep sleep, mistaking the drug’s effects for the exhaustion of the journey.

“So that was why you were outside my room that night.”

“I had to conceal my presence even as I left. That bastard—no, Captain Song—remained awake until dawn despite taking the drug.”

Song Ilseom, leaning against the wall with his arms folded, muttered expressionlessly.

“So that was a mind-clouding drug. No wonder I felt unusually tired that day. Use something better next time—assuming you have a next time.”

*What a goddamn bastard.*

Heo Jun barely swallowed the curse rising to his lips and looked at Ju Hwaran.

“Hwangbo Eom, that old man, threatened me. He said that unless I switched the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, he would kill me and my family and wipe out the Yongbong Escort Bureau. I only wanted to protect everyone!”

“Then you made the wrong choice.”

“You’re right. I even went to my hyung’s[^3] sickbed once and confessed everything in tears. But… but I couldn’t undo my mistake.”

“Your mistake?”

Ju Hwaran’s eyes trembled at the mention of her father, but only for an instant.

Then she gave a small shake of her head.

“No. You’re wrong. It wasn’t a mistake. It was a choice, Uncle.”

“Hwaran…!”

“My father often told me that every choice carries responsibility. Though he failed to make the family business he inherited prosper, he never once regretted the choices he made.”

Heo Jun suddenly realized that the conflict and uncertainty he had seen in Ju Hwaran’s eyes were fading.

*It can’t be.*

No.

It could not be.

This could not be happening!

Tears and cold sweat streamed down Heo Jun’s cheeks.

He desperately raised his voice.

“Give me one chance! Just one last chance! I’m your father’s one and only sworn younger brother, and your uncle, aren’t I? Hwaran, for the sake of the bond we’ve shared, please!”

“The bond we’ve shared, you say?”

“Yes! I shared thirty years of hardship and joy with my hyung.[^3] If your father were here—if it were him—he would not take my life so easily!”

“Uncle Heo. No—Chief Escort Heo Jun.”

Heo Jun stopped pounding his head against the floor and looked up blankly.

His niece’s eyes met his.

They were eyes he had never seen before—cold and utterly devoid of hesitation.

“You’re right. If my father were here, he would have forgiven you. But…”

Her low voice continued toward the frozen Heo Jun.

“I am not Junzi Sword Ju Hogun. I am Dagger Hidden Flower Ju Hwaran.”

The next instant, silver sword light filled Heo Jun’s vision.

Swish! Slice!
